rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God sent Hud to the people of ʿAd as their brother.
rows.anchor: المعنى وأرسلنا إلى عاد أخاهم هودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are Hud's brothers because he was one of them and spoke their language, and because he was a human descendant of Adam like them.
rows.anchor: إحداهما أنه منهم وبين بلسانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayruhu may be an adjective qualifying ilāh; alternatively, the phrase means that they have no god other than Him.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت غيره، غيره من نعت الإله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A drought had afflicted ʿĀd; Hud told them that seeking forgiveness and repenting would bring abundant rain.
rows.anchor: كان أصابهم جدب فاعلمهم أنهم إن استغفروا ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance entails remorse for past sins, resolve not to return to them, and persistence in performing obligatory duties.
rows.anchor: والتوبة الندم على ما سلف، والعزم على ترك العود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madārāran is accusative as a circumstantial expression, as if the wording were that the sky comes pouring.
rows.anchor: ونصب (مدرارا) على الحال، كأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form madārār conveys intensive abundance.
rows.anchor: ومعنى مدرار المبالغة، وكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Hud, ʿĀd, had gardens, crops, and settled cultivation; their homes lay in the sandy region between Syria and Yemen.
rows.anchor: وكان قوم هود - أعني عادا - أهل بساتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud called ʿĀd to monotheism, repentance, and abandoning idols; they refused, persisted in disbelief, and God sent a wind that tore them limb by limb.
rows.anchor: فدعاهم هود إلى توحيد الله واستغفاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind entered their noses, exited through their backsides, and cut them apart limb by limb.
rows.anchor: فكانت تدخل في أنوفهم وتخرج من أدبارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible sense is that God will increase the blessings they already possess.
rows.anchor: أي يزدكم قوة في النعمة التي لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense is that God will increase their bodily strength.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون: ويزدكم قوة في أبدانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people claimed that one of their idols had touched Hud with madness because he had insulted it.
rows.anchor: أي ما نقول إلا مسك بعض أصنامنا بجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger's great sign is to stand alone against a united people and challenge them to scheme without respite, though they cannot harm him.
rows.anchor: وهذه من أعظم آيات الرسل أن يكون الرسول وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud's challenge is compared with Noah's challenge to his people to gather their plans and partners and then act without delay.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قال نوح لقومه: (فأجمعوا

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: Muhammad is quoted as saying, If you have a plan, then scheme against me.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers' ability to issue this challenge is among the greatest and clearest signs of their messengership.
rows.anchor: فهذه هن أعظم آيات الرسل وأدلها على رسالاتهم

words: مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every creature is in God's grasp, and His power can bring it under whatever action He wills.
rows.anchor: أي هي في قبضته، وتنالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God's power reaches creatures as He wills, He wills only what is just.
rows.anchor: أي هو سبحانه وإن كانت قدرته تنالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening means, if you turn away.
rows.anchor: المعنى فإن تتولوا. (فقد أبلغتكم

words: فَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُم مَّآ أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِۦٓ إِلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that Hud has delivered his message establishes the proof against his audience.
rows.anchor: فجعل (فقد أبلغتكم) في موضع قد ثبتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stones' marks identify them as stones with which God punished people.
rows.anchor: بسيماها أنها مما عذب الله بها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the warning to mean that the punishment is not far from the wrongdoers of this community.
rows.anchor: قيل إنها ما هي من ظالمي هذه الأمة ببعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying wording is sent to the people of Midian; the word people is omitted and Midian stands in its place.
rows.anchor: المعنى أرسلنا إلى أهل مدين أخاهم شعيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian may name either the city or the tribe, which explains why it is treated as diptote.
rows.anchor: ومدين اسم المدينة أو القبيلة فلذلك لم ينصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of God's remainder is obedience to God.
rows.anchor: ومعناه طاعة الله (خير لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means the good condition that remains for you.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معناه الحال التي تبقى لكم من الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading is aṣalawātuka, with a long ā in ṣalawāt.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ: أصلواتك. (تأمرك أن نترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their response shows that they worshipped gods other than God.
rows.anchor: هذا دليل أنهم كانوا يعبدون غير الله

words: أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their complaint means that they had agreed among themselves to shortchange in their business dealings.
rows.anchor: المعنى إنا قد تراضينا بالبخس فيما بيننا

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A reported explanation says Shuʿayb forbade them to clip or break coins.
rows.anchor: وفي التفسير أنه نهاهم أن يحذفوا الدراهم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation is that they used praise ironically to mean that he was foolish and ignorant.
rows.anchor: قيل كنى بذا عن أنهم قالوا له:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view is that they said it mockingly.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنهم قالوا له هذا على وجه السخري

words: إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause has no expressed answer because its meaning is understood by the audience.
rows.anchor: وجواب الشرط ههنا متروك. المعنى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of good provision is lawful provision.
rows.anchor: ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is the obedience to which Shuʿayb was enabled.
rows.anchor: وقيل:. رزقا حسنا ما وفق له

words: وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb says he does not forbid something and then do it himself; he chooses for them what he chooses for himself.
rows.anchor: أي لست أنهاكم عن شيء وأدخل فيه

words: أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction means to aim, by acting contrary to someone, at doing the very thing one forbids.
rows.anchor: أي ما أقصد بخلافك القصد إلى أن أرتكبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As much as he is able means his capacity to convey the warning; he cannot compel people to obey.
rows.anchor: أي بقدر طاقتي، وقدر طاقتي إبلاغكم وإنذاركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither Shuʿayb nor anyone else can perform obedience except through God's enabling.
rows.anchor: فأعلم أنه لا يقدر هو ولا غيره على الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anību means that Shuʿayb returns to God.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (إليه أنيب) إليه أرجع

words: أَن يُصِيبَكُم مِّثْلُ مَآ أَصَابَ قَوْمَ نُوحٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause beginning with an is accusative; the sense is that hostility toward Shuʿayb must not bring the people to incur an immediate punishment.
rows.anchor: موضع أن نصب، المعنى لا تكسبنكم عداوتكم

words: قَوْمَ نُوحٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ هُودٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ صَالِحٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb warns them by recalling the punishments of Noah's, Hud's, and Salih's peoples.
rows.anchor: مثل ما أصاب قوم نوح أو قوم هود أو قوم صالح وما قوم لوط منكم ببعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's people suffered the nearest known destruction, so their story is a nearby warning to Shuʿayb's audience.
rows.anchor: وكان إهلاك قوم لوط أقرب الإهلاكات التي عرفوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb was blind; in the Himyar dialect, ḍaʿīf can mean blind, as ḍarīr also describes loss of sight and the resulting inability to act.
rows.anchor: وكان ضريرا. وحمير تسمي المكفوف ضعيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they would have killed him by stoning, regarded as one of the worst killings; his clan shared their religion, so they showed the clan favor and respect.
rows.anchor: أي لولا عشيرتك لرجمناك أي لقتلناك بالرجم

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A reported explanation identifies the true invocation as the testimony that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير: دعوة الحق شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj also allows that the true invocation is a monotheist's prayer to God, which God answers.
rows.anchor: وجائز - والله أعلم - أن تكون دعوة الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols answer no prayers; calling them is like a thirsty person asking water to reach his mouth, though water cannot respond or arrive.
rows.anchor: والماء لا يستجيب، فأعلم الله - عز وجل - أن دعاءهم الأصنام

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another account pictures a person at a well's edge calling water from its bottom to his mouth; Zajjāj says the two explanations amount to the same thing.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: One reported interpretation says believers prostrate willingly and unbelievers unwillingly.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن المؤمن يسجد طوعا

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Another report says some people entered Islam willingly, while others did so only after being threatened with a sword and initially submitted unwillingly.
rows.anchor: وجاء أن من الناس من دخل في الإسلام طوعا ومنهم من لم يدخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj allows that prostration means submission: some accept God's command when easy, while others accept even what they find burdensome.
rows.anchor: وجائز - والله أعلم - أن يكون (طوعا وكرها)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shadows also prostrate to God.
rows.anchor: أي وتسجد ظلالهم. وجاء في التفسير أن الكافر

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A reported explanation says that unbelievers prostrate to other gods while their shadows prostrate to God.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن الكافر يسجد لغير الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view takes their shadows to mean their bodies, which Zajjāj says conflicts with the interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل وظلالهم أشخاصهم، وهذا مخالف للتفسير

words: أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخْلْقِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether anyone besides God created something that could be confused with God's creation.
rows.anchor: أي هل - أو أغير الله خلق شيئا فاشتبه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to declare God creator of everything is supported by the surah's earlier evidence for His oneness, then leads into a parable about believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي قل ذلك وبينه بما أخبر الله به من الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valleys flowed according to the amount God had allotted them to hold; alternatively, the phrase means according to their capacity.
rows.anchor: أي بما قدر لها من ملئها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foam is floating high above the water.
rows.anchor: أي: طافيا عاليا فوق الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means kindling material in pursuit of useful goods.
rows.anchor: أي ابتغاء متاع. (زبد مثله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gold and silver are heated for jewelry; iron, brass, copper, and lead are heated to make useful articles.
rows.anchor: والذي يوقد عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية: الذهب والفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metalwork produces foam like the foam on water.
rows.anchor: و (زبد مثله) أي مثل زبد الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Foam includes water froth and the dross of iron, brass, copper, and lead; it goes away uselessly, cast up by the valley.
rows.anchor: أي: من زبد الماء، والزبد من خبث الحديد

words: وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beneficial water, silver, gold, iron, and other materials listed remain in the earth.
rows.anchor: وأما ما ينفع الناس من الماء والفضة والذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The segment begins to compare the believer, his belief, and faith's benefit to the water in the parable.
rows.anchor: فمثل المؤمن واعتقاده ونفع الإيمان كمثل هذا الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speakers favored the lighter fatḥ in the oath because they swore often by la-ʿamrī and la-ʿumruka; frequent use fixed the easier form.
rows.anchor: آثروا الفتح في القسم لأن الفتح أخف عليهم وهم يكثرون القسم بلعمري

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: Grammarians parse la-ʿumruka as a nominative subject with an omitted predicate, meaning My life is my oath or what I swear by.
rows.anchor: وقال النحويون ارتفع لعمرك بالابتداء والخبر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's verb may be omitted because the hearer understands that the speaker is swearing; the predicate of the subject is likewise omitted.
rows.anchor: وباب القسم قد يحذف معه الفعل، تقول: والله لأفعلن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʿmahūn means that they are bewildered.
rows.anchor: المعنى أقسم إنهم لفي سكرتهم يعمهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cry of punishment seized Lot's people when they encountered sunrise.
rows.anchor: أي أخذت قوم لوط الصيحة بالعذاب مشرقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashraqnā means that people met the sunrise, just as aṣbaḥnā means that they met the morning.
rows.anchor: إذا صادفوا شروق الشمس، وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's rising can be expressed with either sharaqat or ashraqat; here mushriqīn specifically means coinciding with sunrise.
rows.anchor: يقال شرقت الشمس إذا طلعت وأشرقت بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading تنزل الملائكة is reported; Zajjāj also lists ينزل الملائكة, وينزل الملائكة, and وتنزل الملائكة بالروح as possible forms but says he does not know them to have been read.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ: تنزل الملائكة، ويجوز فيها أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit is something from God's command that gives souls life and guides people to God's command.
rows.anchor: والروح - والله أعلم - كان فيه من أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is directed to unbelievers and sinners: affirm God's oneness and do not associate anything with Him.
rows.anchor: المعنى أنذروا أهل الكفر والمعاصي بأنه لا إله إلا أنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above those associated with Him because they create nothing, while the heavens and earth are created.
rows.anchor: ارتفع عن الذين أشركوهم به، لأنهم لا يخلقون شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse abbreviates the account of human development; the Qur'an recounts the changing stages of human life elsewhere.
rows.anchor: اختصر ههنا، وذكر تقلب أحوال الإنسان في غير مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawākhir means ships that travel and cleave through the water.
rows.anchor: معنى (مواخر فيه) جواري تجري جريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawāsi are fixed, firmly grounded mountains.
rows.anchor: (رواسي) جبالا رواسي ثوابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means lest the earth sway or fail to remain stable.
rows.anchor: (أن تميد) معناه كراهة أن تميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Māda al-rajul yamīdu can mean to become dizzy; al-maydā refers to people who become dizzy while riding at sea.
rows.anchor: يقال ماد الرجل يميد ميدا، إذا دير به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause an tamīda is accusative as an object expressing cause.
rows.anchor: (أن تميد) في موضع نصب، مفعول لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense supplies a verb: God placed mountains, rivers, and roads in the earth; alqā here means jaʿala.
rows.anchor: المعنى وجعل فيها رواسي وأنهارا وسبلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation that God placed mountains in the earth is supported by the description of mountains as pegs.
rows.anchor: ودليل ذلك قوله: (والجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent messengers to every community with the command to worship Him.
rows.anchor: فأعلم الله أنه بعث الرسل بالأمر بالعبادة

words: فَمِنْهُم مَّنْ هَدَى ٱللَّهُ وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God stands behind both guidance and misguidance; the verse indicates that those who said so would be truthful if they held the claim as a belief.
rows.anchor: فهذا يدل على أنهم لو قالوا ذلك معتقدين لكانوا صادقين

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَن يَضِلُّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading is given as لا يهدى من يضل, supported by the parallel statement that one whom God leads astray has no guide.
rows.anchor: وقرئت فإن الله لا يهدى من يضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading form, لا يهدي من يضل, is mentioned and judged the least common of the three.
rows.anchor: وفيها وجه ثالث في القراءة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waʿdan is accusative as an emphatic confirmation: God will indeed raise the dead, as a binding promise.
rows.anchor: وعدا) منصوب مؤكد، المعنى بلى يبعثهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible attachment links the purpose clause to resurrection: God raises them to clarify their disagreement and expose disbelievers as liars.
rows.anchor: جائز أن يكون معلقا بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the purpose clause attaches to the sending of a messenger in every community, to clarify their disagreement and prior error.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون (ليبين لهم الذي يختلفون فيه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative yakūnu is the main reading; the accusative yakūna is also read.
rows.anchor: القراءة الرفع، وقد قرئت بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative is explained by an implied huwa: whatever God wills exists.
rows.anchor: القراءة الرفع، وقد قرئت بالنصب، فالرفع على فهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the accusative, yakūna may coordinate with an naqūla, or be an accusative response to the command kun; qawlunā is the subject and an naqūla its predicate.
rows.anchor: والنصب على ضربين أحدهما أن يكون قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording tells people in terms they understand: God's will always comes to be, instantly if He wishes, even though creation is described in familiar speech.
rows.anchor: وهذا خوطب العباد فيه بما يعقلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God possesses knowledge of the unseen in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: ومعناه - والله أعلم -: ولله علم غيب السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is the death of creatures and their being brought back to life.
rows.anchor: والساعة اسم لإماتة الخلق وإحيائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison does not say the Hour will arrive in less than a blink; it describes how swiftly God's power can bring it about.
rows.anchor: فأعلم الله - عز وجل - أن البعث والإحياء في قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form immahātikum is vocalized with kasra; the original plural is amāt, with hā added for emphasis, as in ahrāqtu from araqtu.
rows.anchor: و (إمهاتكم) - بالكسر -، والأصل في الأمهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afʾida is the plural of fuʾād, like aghriba is the plural of غراب.
rows.anchor: والأفئدة جمع فؤاد مثل غراب وأغربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fuʾād is not given a further plural of the larger-count pattern; one does not say fuʾdān, just as the pattern is not used for غراب.
rows.anchor: ولم يجمع فؤاد على أكثر العدد، لم يقل فئدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suspended birds then serve as visible evidence of God's power over the Hour.
rows.anchor: ثم دلهم - سبحانه - على قدرته على أمر الساعة بما شاهدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jaww of the sky is the air far above the earth; al-sakāk is still farther from earth.
rows.anchor: (جو السماء) الهواء البعيد من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj equates al-sakāk with al-lawḥ and gives sakkāka as its singular.
rows.anchor: ومثل السكاك اللوح، وواحد السكاك سكاكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭuwā is the name of the valley.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (طوى). اسم الوادي، ويجوز فيه أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four forms are allowed: Ṭuwā with initial ḍamma, with or without nunation, and with initial kasra, with or without nunation.
rows.anchor: ويجوز فيه أربعة أوجه: طوى - بضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When nunated, Ṭuwā is a masculine valley name on the pattern fuʿal, like Ḥuṭam and Ṣurad.
rows.anchor: فمن نونه فهو اسم الوادي، وهو مذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A non-nunated form may be diptote because it is shifted from Ṭāʾ, like ʿUmar from ʿĀmir, or because it is a place name.
rows.anchor: ومن لم ينونه ترك صرفه من جهتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With initial kasra and nunation it declines like maʿan or ḍilʿ; without nunation it is treated as a place name.
rows.anchor: والجهة الأخرى أن يكون اسما للبقعة كما قال الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is wa-anā ikhtarnāka, We chose you.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (وأنا اخترناك)، فمن قرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For wa-innā ikhtarnāka, the initial clause may be a resumption or quoted speech, reporting that Moses was told, We chose you.
rows.anchor: ويجوز (وإنا اخترناك) على وجهين: على الاستئناف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation of Moses coming at the appointed measure is that he came at the appointed time.
rows.anchor: قيل في التفسير: على موعد، وقيل على قدر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that he came at the measure of God's speaking to him.
rows.anchor: وقيل على قدر من تكليمي إياك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waniyā means do not weaken or slacken; the verb waniya and the expression tawānā describe becoming lax and weak.
rows.anchor: معناه ولا تضعفا، يقال: ونى يني ونيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿalla denotes hope and expectation in ordinary language.
rows.anchor: لعل في اللغة ترج وطمع، تقول: لعلي أصير إلى خير

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh explains the wording as Go, with your hope and expectation.
rows.anchor: والمعنى عند سيبويه فيه: اذهبا على رجائكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God knew Pharaoh would not remember or fear, the messengers had to make the proof clear; the obligation follows from clarification and evidence.
rows.anchor: وقد علم الله عز وجل أنه لا يتذكر ولا يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers do not know the unseen or whether people will accept them; their real hope is part of how they are sent, and God's knowledge is not human knowledge that establishes proof.
rows.anchor: وإنما تبعث الرسل وهي لا تعلم الغيب ولا تدري أيقبل منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hope expressed here is the pattern on which all messengers are sent.
rows.anchor: فمعنى: (لعله يتذكر أو يخشى). هو الذي عليه بعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording kīdu sāḥir is read; Zajjāj also allows kīdu siḥr, and says the accusative opening annamā is not known to him as a reading here; the kasra reading is stronger in meaning.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (كيد سحر)، ويجوز إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the nominative analysis, mā is the subject of inna and kīdu sāḥir is its predicate: what they made is a magician's plot.
rows.anchor: فأما رفع كيد فعلى معنى أن الذي صنعوه كيد ساحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the accusative analysis, mā prevents inna from governing, and kīda is the object of ṣanaʿū, as in innamā ḍarabtu Zaydan.
rows.anchor: كما تقول: إنما ضربت زيدا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation of ḥaythu atā is wherever the magician may be.
rows.anchor: قالوا معناه حيث كان، وقيل معناه حيث كان الساحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that a magician must be killed is also the position of jurists on sorcerers.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه حيث كان الساحر يجب أن يقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original form was khawfah; wāw changed to yāʾ because the preceding letter had kasra.
rows.anchor: وأصلها خوفة، ولكن الواو قلبت ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talaqqaf in the jussive is the reading as an answer to the command; a nominative form is possible as a circumstantial expression but was not read and should not be recited without an established reading.
rows.anchor: وألق ما في يمينك تلقف ما صنعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujjadan is accusative as a circumstantial expression and describes an expected state: they fell intending to prostrate, before they were yet prostrating.
rows.anchor: (سجدا) منصوب على الحال، وهي أيضا حال مقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī means on the palm trunks; it is also apt because the condemned would be lengthwise along and enclosed by the trunk.
rows.anchor: (ولأصلبنكم في جذوع) معناه على جذوع النخل

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb's line uses fī jadʿi nakhlah for being fixed on a palm trunk, illustrating the preposition's sense.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: وهم صلبوا العبدي في جذع نخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyunā is nominative because it stands as an interrogative; the preceding declarative clause cannot govern it.
rows.anchor: رفعت لأنها وضعت موضع الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhī is genitive in the sense that they will not prefer Pharaoh to God.
rows.anchor: موضع الذي خفض، المعنى لن نؤثرك على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, alladhī is genitive as an oath: they swear by God.
rows.anchor: خفضا على القسم، ويكون المعنى لن نؤثرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means, do what you are going to do.
rows.anchor: أي: اصنع ما أنت صانع، قال أبو ذؤيب

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb uses qaḍāhumā to mean that the two garments were made or fashioned.
rows.anchor: قال أبو ذؤيب: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥayāta al-dunyā is read in the accusative; a nominative is possible, though Zajjāj knows no one who read it.
rows.anchor: القراءة بالنصب - الحياة الدنيا - ويجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the nominative, the meaning is that what Pharaoh adjudicates is only the enjoyment of worldly life.
rows.anchor: تأويله أن الذي تقضيه متاع الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwājan here means men from among them.
rows.anchor: أي رجالا منهم. (زهرة الحياة الدنيا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zahrah is given with either fatḥa or sukūn on the hāʾ.
rows.anchor: و (زهرة) جميعا - بفتح الهاء وتسكينها - و (زهرة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zahrata is accusative as the object or result of mattaʿnā, meaning God made worldly life a bloom for them.
rows.anchor: و (زهرة) منصوب بمعنى متعنا لأن معناه جعلنا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is to make that worldly provision a trial for them.
rows.anchor: لنفتنهم فيه). أي لنجعل ذلك فتنة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request means why does he not bring a sign; signs had already come, but they wanted to prescribe which signs would support them.
rows.anchor: معناه هلا يأتينا بآية أمن ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs are also allowed in the passive forms yudhalla and yukhzā.
rows.anchor: من قبل أن نذل ونخزى). يجوز فيها يذل ويخزى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reckoning has drawn near for people; more precisely, the time of their reckoning is near.
rows.anchor: معناه اقتربت القيامة، ومثله: (اقتربت الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive muḥdathin is the reading; outside the reading, muḥdathan in the accusative as a circumstantial expression and muḥdathun in the nominative with an implied huwa are possible.
rows.anchor: الخفض القراءة، ويجوز في غير القراءة (محدثا ومحدث)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lāhiyatan qulūbuhum can coordinate with the sense of listening while playing, meaning that they listened playfully.
rows.anchor: لاهية قلوبهم) معطوف على معنى (إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, lāhiyatan qulūbuhum is accusative governed by yalʿabūn.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون (لاهية قلوبهم) منصوبا بقوله (يلعبون)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best analysis makes alladhīna nominative as an appositive to the plural subject of asarrū, clarifying who the subject is.
rows.anchor: في (أسروا) قولان أجودهما أن يكون (الذين ظلموا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes alladhīna nominative as a reproach, meaning they are the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون رفعا على الذم على معنى هم الذين ظلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis makes alladhīna accusative, with an implied aʿnī, I mean the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب على معنى أعني الذين ظلموا
